card: Makes addrman address sampling inside buckets uniformly random across occupied slots. Previously, bucket selection began at a random offset and took the next occupied position, heavily biasing peer selection toward addresses following large runs of empty positions (such as 95.3% versus 4.7% in a two-entry bucket). The PR gathers occupied slots into a local buffer, samples uniformly while filtering by network, and adds chi-square uniformity unit tests and fuzz checks.
changed_since_previous: No substantial changes to the approach or test coverage; minor patch updates or rebase.
evidence: PR description calculates the exact bias: 'if for example only position 17 and 20 contain an address, 17 will be picked with probability 95.3% (whenever the initial position is 21..63 or 0..17) and 20 will be picked with probability 4.7% (whenever the initial position is 18..20).'
PR description notes the issue was previously raised by mzumsande (PR #23140 review) and Crypt-iQ.
problem: Addrman bucket selection previously used a linear scan starting at a random offset among the 64 bucket positions. In sparse buckets, this heavily biased selection toward entries located after long gaps of empty positions (for example, 95.3% versus 4.7% in a bucket with only two entries), skewing peer connection selection.

risk.why: Flaws in addrman address selection could cause infinite loops, crash the node, or degrade peer selection diversity and eclipse resistance.

summary: Switches address selection within an addrman bucket to uniform random sampling over all occupied slots. Rather than picking a random starting position and linearly scanning to the next occupied entry, occupied entries are copied into a stack buffer and chosen uniformly at random while respecting any network filter. A unit test using a chi-square test and an invariant check in the addrman fuzz target verify the uniform distribution and filter compliance.
